key_insight: λ-MACE enables experimentally accurate hydration free energies, but combining hydration and sublimation predictions still leaves crystalline solubility errors above experimental uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This physics-based workflow could support drug formulation and solubility assessment, though crystalline thermodynamics needs greater accuracy before reliable deployment.
method: Use λ-MACE, a machine learning interatomic potential optimized for condensed-phase free energy calculations.
Compute hydration and sublimation free energies within a free energy perturbation workflow.
Combine both thermodynamic legs to predict neutral-molecule solubility from known experimental crystal structures.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 70 medicinally relevant FreeSolv compounds for hydration and 10 additional compounds for crystalline solubility, with overall solubility accuracy of 1.53 log units versus experimental accuracy of 0.17–0.6 log units.
watch_item: Closing the solubility accuracy gap requires roughly 0.5 kcal/mol accuracy in each thermodynamic leg, with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest remaining challenge.
paper_title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE
